headline: ACC starts investigation against Asif Mahmud and 3 others over corruption
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission has launched a probe into allegations of corruption involving the former advisor.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has initiated an investigation into former advisor Asif Mahmud Sajib Bhuiyan and three others following allegations of corruption.
The decision to probe the matter was confirmed by an ACC spokesperson, indicating that the commission is looking into the claims of financial irregularities.
Asif Mahmud served as an advisor to the interim government, and the investigation aims to determine the validity of the corruption charges.
The probe will examine the roles of the individuals involved and the nature of the allegations to ensure accountability.
caption:
The Anti-Corruption Commission is probing former advisor Asif Mahmud and three others over corruption allegations.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has initiated an investigation into former advisor Asif Mahmud Sajib Bhuiyan and three others following allegations of corruption.

Asif Mahmud served as an advisor to the interim government, and the investigation aims to determine the validity of the corruption charges.

The probe will examine the roles of the individuals involved and the nature of the allegations to ensure accountability.

headline_marked: Power crisis to [[improve within 15 days]], says State Minister
headline: Power crisis to improve within 15 days, says State Minister
summary: State Minister Aninda Islam Amit acknowledges policy failures and technical faults as causes for recent shortages, promising a quicker resolution.
details: State Minister for Power and Energy Aninda Islam Amit told Parliament that the country's power situation is expected to improve noticeably within the next 15 days.
The Minister apologised to the nation for the public suffering caused by electricity and gas shortages in August, attributing the crisis to long-standing policy failures and Middle East tensions.
Technical issues were a major factor, with a 616MW unit of the Payra Power Plant and a unit of the Matarbari Power Plant currently offline for maintenance or faults.
The government is also facing supply gaps from India's Adani Group, receiving only 900-1,100MW daily despite a contracted agreement for 1,600MW.
LNG supply disruptions caused by technical faults in two floating storage regasification units (FSRUs) further pressured the energy system.
To prevent future crises, the government is pursuing long-term initiatives like rooftop solar projects and diversifying energy import sources beyond the Middle East.
Addressing billing complaints, the Minister admitted to some errors and proposed the nationwide installation of smart prepaid meters as the permanent solution.
caption:
Bangladesh's power situation is expected to improve in 15 days, according to the State Minister.

State Minister for Power and Energy Aninda Islam Amit told Parliament that the country's power situation is expected to improve noticeably within the next 15 days.

The Minister apologised to the nation for the public suffering caused by electricity and gas shortages in August, attributing the crisis to long-standing policy failures and Middle East tensions.

Technical issues were a major factor, with a 616MW unit of the Payra Power Plant and a unit of the Matarbari Power Plant currently offline for maintenance or faults.

The government is also facing supply gaps from India's Adani Group, receiving only 900-1,100MW daily despite a contracted agreement for 1,600MW.

LNG supply disruptions caused by technical faults in two floating storage regasification units (FSRUs) further pressured the energy system.

To prevent future crises, the government is pursuing long-term initiatives like rooftop solar projects and diversifying energy import sources beyond the Middle East.

Addressing billing complaints, the Minister admitted to some errors and proposed the nationwide installation of smart prepaid meters as the permanent solution.
